abaeed47-79ca-4048-b758-2ebe3c9da5c3.hook_pattern: Historical enumeration list + contrarian reframe + punchy closing kicker
abaeed47-79ca-4048-b758-2ebe3c9da5c3.hook_template: Every crypto cycle had its 'this kills it.' [Year] — [fear]. [Year] — [fear]. [Year] — [fear]. Now: [current fear]. [Memorable one-liner prediction.]
abaeed47-79ca-4048-b758-2ebe3c9da5c3.structural_lesson: Stack 3-5 historical fears in rapid list format to trigger pattern recognition. Each item proves the recurring structure. The final item is the present. Close with a confident, almost flippant prediction — the brevity signals certainty. No hedge, no explanation. The list does the persuasion.

5c49ac7a-5a01-4aa9-9aa6-c6fac12cd8e6.hook_pattern: Side-by-side visual comparison + shared cultural grievance + participatory mockery
5c49ac7a-5a01-4aa9-9aa6-c6fac12cd8e6.hook_template: Companies are replacing [real thing] with AI-generated [thing]. Here's what that looks like. [Side-by-side image]. The internet has opinions.
5c49ac7a-5a01-4aa9-9aa6-c6fac12cd8e6.psychological_trigger: Shared outrage + humor + collective identity protection (we can see through this) + universal relevance (everyone eats)
5c49ac7a-5a01-4aa9-9aa6-c6fac12cd8e6.structural_lesson: The mockery wave format: a single comparison image that crystallizes a broader frustration generates outsized engagement because it gives people a clear, shareable artifact to pile onto. The poster's own opinion barely matters — the image IS the content. AI food photos worked at 13M+ views because food is universal, the images were visually wrong in ways everyone could see, and it invited participation (quote-tweet your local restaurant's AI photos). The participatory element is the multiplier.

4f8b3bcf-0d42-42c2-8999-6aea5403edcc.hook_pattern: Meta-contrarian: reframe the prevailing viral narrative as a commercial or strategic move
4f8b3bcf-0d42-42c2-8999-6aea5403edcc.hook_template: Everyone is sharing [person]'s [scary warning]. What they're not saying: [alternative explanation that reframes it as self-interest/marketing/strategy].
4f8b3bcf-0d42-42c2-8999-6aea5403edcc.psychological_trigger: Intellectual superiority (I see what others miss) + cynicism-validation + anti-groupthink identity
4f8b3bcf-0d42-42c2-8999-6aea5403edcc.structural_lesson: The second-order contrarian: when a post goes massively viral, there is always a second wave of high-engagement posts that question the motives behind it. The Fortune 'AI doomsday as sales pitch' angle on Jacob Coxon's thread is a classic example. It requires no original research — just a reframe. Works best as a single short tweet. Must name the viral post by implication (don't quote it, let the reader connect the dots). Cynicism resonates with the sophisticated-insider identity that crypto and AI Twitter cultivates.

dcbc86c9-d939-4f1f-a5fa-42894d4bd513.hook_pattern: Insider resignation + credentialed doomsday warning + reluctance signal + career sacrifice as authenticity marker
dcbc86c9-d939-4f1f-a5fa-42894d4bd513.hook_template: I spent [X years] at [major AI lab]. I'm leaving. I need to tell you what I saw. [First scary claim.]
dcbc86c9-d939-4f1f-a5fa-42894d4bd513.psychological_trigger: Epistemic fear + institutional betrayal + insider credibility + sacrifice-as-sincerity signal
dcbc86c9-d939-4f1f-a5fa-42894d4bd513.structural_lesson: The whistleblower template: open with years spent and institution name (credibility), signal the resignation (sacrifice = proof of sincerity), lead immediately into the claim. The more specific the claim, the higher the reach. The author having never tweeted before amplified authenticity. 90M+ views in 24 hours and 170M+ in 10 days show the ceiling on this format in AI discourse. Evan Hubinger's public backing as a named expert doubled the second-wave engagement.

de9ffeeb-3c76-4c5d-8bf9-f17bb83c6421.hook_template: I built [X]. Today, [X] is [ending/joining/changing]. Here is what that means for everyone who used it — and what comes next.
de9ffeeb-3c76-4c5d-8bf9-f17bb83c6421.psychological_trigger: Community identity threat + nostalgia + pragmatic concern + curiosity (what happens to my project?)
de9ffeeb-3c76-4c5d-8bf9-f17bb83c6421.structural_lesson: The 'I built this and now it's over' announcement is one of the highest-engagement formats in developer/tech Twitter. Ryan Dahl's Cloudflare/Deno announcement worked because Deno had a passionate community. The formula: Creator's voice (not corporate), acknowledge the community's investment first, explain the decision second, give a concrete migration timeline third. The thread replies are the real content — the original tweet is a catalyst for community-generated engagement. Developer communities reshare these at extremely high rates.

fd582c84-4cae-4fb8-a9b1-0a0a646569d1.hook_pattern: Hidden-danger-in-trusted-product reveal + visual proof + supply chain fear
fd582c84-4cae-4fb8-a9b1-0a0a646569d1.hook_template: I found something inside my [trusted device] that should not be there. [Short description of what it is.] [Photo/video of the evidence.]
fd582c84-4cae-4fb8-a9b1-0a0a646569d1.psychological_trigger: Security fear + institutional betrayal + physical evidence (irrefutable) + everyone-is-vulnerable implication
fd582c84-4cae-4fb8-a9b1-0a0a646569d1.structural_lesson: The physical proof post: one of the highest-engagement crypto formats. Short text — the image carries the message. The hook must imply 'this affects you too' without saying it. Include the word 'inside' or equivalent. Visual evidence short-circuits skepticism. The discovery narrative (I noticed X, then found Y) beats the announcement narrative (Company did X). Ledger/CryptoBilis supply chain hack generated massive secondary commentary and trust collapse discourse — the original photos/videos of hardware implants seeded hundreds of quote tweets.

14786cfb-5619-4849-a3de-284d148c037f.hook_pattern: Adversity stack + age paradox + institution rejection + eventual proof
14786cfb-5619-4849-a3de-284d148c037f.hook_template: Rejected by [N] [institutions]. Built [X] anyway. [Exit outcome]. Now building [Y]. Here's what I learned institutions can't teach you:
14786cfb-5619-4849-a3de-284d148c037f.psychological_trigger: Underdog sympathy + gatekeeping outrage + aspirational FOMO + identity validation for non-traditional paths
14786cfb-5619-4849-a3de-284d148c037f.structural_lesson: The rejection-to-success founder narrative works best when the rejection count is absurdly specific (15 universities, not 'many'). The arc must be fast: rejection → build → win → next thing. Never dwell on the rejection — one sentence max. The asymmetry (rejected by 15, raised $10M by 19) is the content. Ending with a 'lessons learned' thread structure invites broad resharing because it packages aspiration as education.
